The **re-operation rate** (*re-operationsrate*) is a critical quality parameter used to monitor and evaluate the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in Denmark. Within the institutional framework of DANIBD—the national clinical quality database for IBD—this metric serves as a key operational measurement to ensure equitable, evidence-based care across different regions and hospital departments. 

The metric is closely monitored by the [[styregruppen-for-danibd|Styregruppen for DANIBD]], which holds the responsibility for assessing and implementing clinical indicators. The steering committee has identified the re-operation rate as a significant operational challenge, explicitly concluding that the rate is generally too high [^src1]. Because of this assessment, the metric functions as a direct trigger for quality improvement interventions: departments exhibiting high re-operation values are subject to recommendations for internal audits to investigate underlying causes, which may include clinical shortcomings or administrative coding errors. 

This parameter is evaluated as part of DANIBD's broader quality monitoring narrative, alongside other vital clinical indicators such as systematic colonoscopies for patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) to prevent colorectal cancer [^src1].
